open_obligations: Note that the judges are LLMs, and check whether the errors here are the kind of misleading errors Wen et al. call for evaluating.
Check whether consultant training here is analogous to RLHF in Wen et al.
Check whether debate actually reduced false positives on incorrect answers.
out.other_title: Do scalable oversight methods (critique, debate, decomposition) work on misleading errors?
out.rationale: Wen et al. ask whether scalable oversight methods such as debate work against misleading errors. Arnesen et al. report trained debaters add 96% more quoted words and their win rates transfer between judges (correlation 0.98), while trained consultants' transfer only at 0.51, which the authors read as consultants learning features idiosyncratically convincing to their judge; the judges are LLMs (a trained GPT-4-Turbo judge and an untrained GPT-4o judge).
out.scope: proposed ADDRESSES: whether debate resists the judge-specific persuasion that one-sided optimisation learns, for trained Llama3-8B debaters and consultants

text: The paper reports the fully trained debate model's speeches contain 96% more quoted words than the SFT model, whereas the final consultant uses 70% fewer quotes (barely significant) and repeats 98% of its second-speech quoted material from its first speech. Win rates under the trained GPT-4-Turbo judge and an untrained GPT-4o judge correlate at 0.98 for debaters but only 0.51 for consultants, which the authors read as consultants learning features idiosyncratically convincing to the judge they were optimised against.
title: Debate training adds quoted evidence and transfers to GPT-4o; consultancy does not
